html:
In the election of 31 October 1991, Zambians voted out President Kenneth Kaunda and elected the trade union leader Frederick Chiluba. It was one of the first times in Africa that a founding president lost power at the ballot box and stepped down.

Food riots and an attempted coup in 1990, and the end of the Cold War, had pushed Kaunda to restore multiparty politics. Chiluba's Movement for Multi-Party Democracy won a landslide.

Kaunda's quick acceptance of defeat set an example across the continent. Chiluba's government sold off the copper mines and other state firms, but became known for corruption. Zambia has since seen several peaceful changes of ruling party.
